name: Medina of Tunis
subtitle: A cultural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1979.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “Under the Almohads and the Hafsids, from the 12th to the 16th century, Tunis was considered one of the greatest and wealthiest cities in the Islamic world. Some 700 monuments, including palaces, mosques, mausoleums, madrasas and fountains, testify to this remarkable past.”
The Medina of Tunis has been a World Heritage Site since 1979 and contains some 700 monuments, including palaces, mosques, mausoleums, madrasas and fountains, according to Wikipedia.

The article says it was founded in 698 around the original core of the Zitouna Mosque and took its essential form in the Hafsid period, when Tunis became a religious, intellectual and economic centre.

sections.title: A living medina, as reported in 2022

parts.text: Africanews reported in July 2022 that the medina was founded in the ninth century and began to expand in the 13th, when Tunis became the capital of the Hafsid kingdom. It has about two dozen small souks devoted to artisans such as tanners, perfume sellers and shoemakers, and was listed in 1979.

About 25,000 people live in the medina. New initiatives bring in art festivals, guesthouses and a project offering treasure hunts, cooking classes and calligraphy. The report adds that some museums and monuments remain closed, including the Sidi Bou Khrissane and Dar Ben Abdallah museums, closed for 15 years, and that the Zitouna mosque is closed to non-Muslims.

gaps: Residents' and craftspeople's accounts of the medina today.
The Ottoman and French periods, which the part of the article read here does not reach.
Residents' accounts of the changes, and of the houses and crafts, are not here. The July 2022 figures are the report's.
